draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s28fp-1919-b1 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 81% of its fill; s28fp-1919-b1 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 2 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 81% of its fill; s28fp-1919-b1 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 3 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 81% of its fill. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row '(default)' overlaid with the frontage row: 2½S.B.: two full storeys and a half in the roof, read as gabled dormers in a hip over the post-1902 enlargement; the projecting tower/bay is T-1906's. The 1911 sheet's Gatlin Institute is a 1911 use and is not carried back. The sheet traces the house and its rear range as one part, whose largest rectangle is a 47 m strip down the lot; the main body is fitted in front of the part's own break at 21.3 m from the rear lot line, where it narrows to the street front, and the rear range behind it. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 465919014 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet labels the building with a 1911 use, '2½S.B. brick The Gatlin Institute', which the draft does not carry back to 1904 (the T-1837 register warns not to assume the 1904 use from it). The register's family row, 'Field Jr., post-1902 enlargement', names it a house, so the 1904 function is inferred residence on that row and the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on
